notifications.title: New Task: Summative Assessment (Unit II)
notifications.detail:
Vaishali Rajasekaran has just added a new Task Summative Assessment (Unit II) in IB MYP Individuals and Societies (MYP Year 1) C.
When: September 8, 2026 at 8:00 AM
Task Overview
You are a City Planner hired by a local government. Your mission is to investigate how a settlement changes over time and present a realistic redesign proposal that meets community needs sustainably. 
(Example: You can choose a certain city such as Hyderabad, Chennai or Bangalore and propose redesigning ideas to deal with monsoon flooding etc.)
Role & Scenario You are a City Planner. A local government wants to redesign a fast-growing settlement (you can choose a real city/town like Hyderabad, Tokyo or your hometown or any city, town or village that you are particularly curious about).
The settlement is growing because more people are moving there and the population is increasing. As the settlement grows, it may face problems such as:
Traffic and transportation

Lack of housing

Less green space

Pressure on resources

Loss of historical places and culture

Social inequality

Growth of informal settlements

and many more….

Your role is to create a  Settlement Research & Redesign Blueprint.Your blueprint will have two parts: 
Part 1: The Investigation Journal (Criteria B)

Part 2: The Critical Urban Proposal (Criteria D)

Part 1: The Investigation Journal (Criteria B)
Students will create a booklet and include the following information:
Identify a city/area of your choice of a fast growing settlement 

Identify the research question 

List the climate, natural features, population size

Describe a brief historical development of the chosen location/area (include a timeline to record key events related to the place from the beginning till now)

Outline important events in detailed examples such as; Why did it occur? Who was responsible for it and how did it change the place?

Identify two strengths (What makes it a good settlement? Refer to settlement functions).

Identify two limitations (What are the problems regularly occurring in this settlement? What is the cause)

G – Goal
To write an engaging beginning for an original fantasy story that introduces a character inspired by mythology, establishes the setting, and hints at a present-day conflict.
Your writing should capture the reader's interest while demonstrating effective narrative organization and language use.
R – Role
You are a creative author who has been invited to contribute the opening chapter of a new fantasy story for a children's magazine titled "Legends Reawakened."
A – Audience
Your audience is young readers aged 10–13 who enjoy stories filled with mystery, adventure, courage, and mythical elements.
S – Situation
The editor of "Legends Reawakened" is looking for stories that connect ancient myths with modern life.
Imagine a bustling modern city where people have stopped paying attention to old stories and legends. As a result, mysterious events have begun to occur. One day, an ordinary young person discovers that they are connected to an ancient mythical guardian whose powers have been asleep for centuries.
You have been asked to write only the beginning of the story, introducing the main character and setting while creating curiosity about the strange events affecting the city.
P – Product
Write an original 200–250-word beginning of a story that includes:
An engaging hook 
Introduction of the main character 
A vivid setting 
Clear use of sensory details 
A hint of a present-day conflict linked to an ancient myth (without resolving it) 
Appropriate narrative language and organization 
S – Success Criteria
Your writing will be successful if it:
Captures the reader's attention from the start 
Clearly introduces the character and setting 
Uses descriptive and sensory language effectively 
Connects mythology with a modern-day situation 
Creates curiosity about the conflict 
Demonstrates accurate grammar, spelling, and punctuation 
Organizes ideas logically and effectively within 200–250 words

Answer key-

1. Why do solids keep their shape while liquids and gases do not?
Solids keep their shape because their particles are tightly packed and can only vibrate in one place. Liquids and gases do not have a fixed shape because their particles can move around.
2. Which state of matter has particles that move the fastest? Explain why.
Gases have particles that move the fastest because they are far apart and have the most energy, allowing them to move freely in all directions.
3. Give one example from your daily life for each state of matter.
Solid: Pencil
Liquid: Water
Gas: Air
4. What would happen to ice if it is left outside on a hot day? Explain the change of state.
Ice would melt and change from a solid to a liquid. This change of state is called melting because the ice absorbs heat from its surroundings.

discussions.title: LAUNCH LAB 2026
discussions.detail:
LAUNCH LAB 2026 Information for the students who are participating: Please go through the following instructions carefully and make sure to follow all the guidelines for your Graphic Design submission.
GRAPHIC DESIGN — GRADE 6 (CBSE, CIE & MYP)
Requirements
Format: JPEG, PNG or PDF

Guidelines
Dimensions / Size: A4 size paper (Portrait or Landscape).

Required Details: At the bottom-left corner of your design, you must include:
Your Name(s)

Your Curriculum

Your House Name

Photo & Quality Guidelines
Image Clarity: Ensure you capture and upload clear, high-quality images of your work. Pictures should not be blurred.

No Watermarks: Photos containing watermarks (e.g., camera or app watermarks) will result in a deduction of marks.

Originality & Copyright
Use only royalty-free images or your own drawings.

Do not copy and paste uncredited images from Google.

The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to generate any images, elements, or text for your poster is strictly prohibited.

Logistical Information
File Naming Convention: Save your file as: Curriculum_Gr6_Groupnumber_House
Example: CBSE_Gr6_Group1_peagsus.pdf
Submission Method: Download the final poster as a JPEG, PNG, or PDF and email it to:
Tgscreativeconquest@thegaudium.com
Resources to Learn Graphic Design
Canva Design School: https://www.canva.com/designschool/

Pixlr Learn: https://pixlr.com/learn/

You are a City Planner hired by a local government. Your mission is to investigate how a settlement changes over time and present a realistic redesign proposal that meets community needs sustainably.

Traffic and transportation

Lack of housing

Less green space

Pressure on resources

Loss of historical places and culture

Social inequality

Growth of informal settlements

and many more….
